before: A*-R, C-FF, and IDFF completed all agents in all 48 blocks of every main movement condition, with zero critical movement violations. Their simulated completion times were identical within each condition and ranged from 4.10 to 11.84 s (Table 5). D*L completed all agents in the four four-neighbor conditions, but failed all-agent completion in the four eight-neighbor conditions, covering 192 blocks. Those blocks contained 1,680 illegal_or_invalid_plan records, which combine unsuccessful planner status and adapter legality rejection. The archived output does not retain these two failure sources separately. The failures describe the frozen movement implementation; SMSB used a later D*L revision with a documented key-comparison correction (Supplementary Section S3).
after: A*-R, C-FF, and IDFF completed all agents in all 48 blocks of every main movement condition, with zero critical movement violations. Their simulated completion times were identical within each condition and ranged from 4.10 to 11.84 s (Table 5). D*L completed all agents in the four four-neighbor conditions, but failed all-agent completion in the four eight-neighbor conditions, covering 192 blocks. Those blocks contained 1,680 illegal_or_invalid_plan records, which combine unsuccessful planner status and adapter legality rejection.  Source-level replay reproduced the failed-agent identities and attributed the reproduced failures to premature termination of D*L repair under exact key comparison. before: Movement evaluation covers completion and path length after a same-tick block/unblock pair, with no intervening movement step and all successful runs ending before the later cost changes. The D*L eight-neighbor failures remain specific to the frozen movement build; the available records do not establish whether the subsequent key-comparison correction resolves them. The callback lane is a main-loop diagnostic. Application-level display timing and sustained dynamic movement would extend this evidence to longer-running interactive scenarios.
after: Movement evaluation covers short trajectories after same-tick blocking and unblocking on disjoint footprints; successful runs end before the later cost changes. The D*L results remain specific to the frozen implementation. Source-level diagnostic replay supports the key-comparison correction, but does not replace the original application timing experiment. The callback lane is a main-loop diagnostic. Application-level display timing and longer-running dynamic movement remain extensions.

before: The movement schedule applies an ordered block/unblock pair within tick 10 (0.20 s), increases traversal costs at 30 s, decreases them at 90 s, and restores the initial state at 150 s. Both initial changes are applied before movement resumes at that tick. Successful runs finish by 11.84 s and therefore cover the initial pair, with no movement step between blocking and restoration; they do not exercise the later cost changes. Arrival is latched when an agent remains within 0.75 cell size of the shared goal center, in the goal cell, for ten consecutive fixed ticks. At each event, the grid, planner, and rendered-world versions must agree.

before: For D*L, main conditions C03, C04, C07, and C08 each have 48 blocks without all-agent completion; their InvalidPlan totals are 48, 48, 1,008, and 576 (1,680 in total). The frozen movement adapter assigns both unsuccessful planner status and rejected returned paths to InvalidPlan, so their separate counts cannot be recovered from these outputs. A later SMSB qualification record, completed on 17 October 2026, documents a D*L key-control comparison correction: an exact lexicographic comparison could stop repair while the primary-key difference lay within the specified 1e-12 equality tolerance. SMSB binds the corrected DStarLitePlanner.cs (SHA-256 prefix b6938a3389de), whereas movement retains its earlier standalone build. This later diagnostic does not establish the cause of every movement failure, and no corrected-build movement sensitivity result is reported here.
after: For D*L, main conditions C03, C04, C07, and C08 each have 48 blocks without all-agent completion; their InvalidPlan totals are 48, 48, 1,008, and 576 (1,680 in total). The archived adapter combines unsuccessful planner status and rejected returned paths in InvalidPlan. A subsequent source-level diagnostic recovered the historical DStarLitePlanner.cs byte-for-byte (SHA-256 prefix ae9f1bdc2a30), matching both the four-method manifests and the movement design contract. Replaying one deterministic trajectory set for each of the eight main movement conditions reproduced every failed-agent identity present in all 384 archived blocks. The replay separated the combined category into 1, 1, 21, and 12 planner InternalError results for C03, C04, C07, and C08, respectively, with no rejected successful paths. These are reconstructed diagnostic classifications; the original records retain their combined category.

The historical repair loop compares priority keys exactly, although its g/rhs consistency test uses a 1e-12 tolerance. In a single-agent reproduction from core-r03-s1-shared (agent 55, start (63, 62), goal (14, 16)), the leading key differed by 1.42e-14 while the secondary key required further processing. Repair stopped and path extraction reached its step limit. The tolerance-aware revision (SHA-256 prefix b6938a3389de), already used by SMSB, changes only the two algorithm-control comparisons and their helper. With that revision, the eight movement replays produced 1,024 arrivals and zero InternalError results across 2,048 plan calls. In 53 fixed-start scenarios, the historical source reproduced all 335 failed query identities sampled across the scenarios, whose per-scenario status totals were identical over all 48 archived repetitions. The corrected source reduced InternalError from 335 to zero across 21,325 calls; successes increased from 20,954 to 21,261 and no-path results from 36 to 64. All 64 corrected no-path query identities matched archived A*-R results, and all returned successful paths passed legality checks. These functional checks ran under the installed Unity distribution's Mono runtime using the frozen scenario, grid, event and movement logic. They do not constitute a new standalone-Player performance acquisition or a full optimal-cost oracle test. The historical Player binary was unavailable at its recorded path, so the original timing results and their implementation identity remain unchanged.

before: The movement experiment schedules five changes in a maximum 180 s simulated window: block and unblock the footprint at tick 10 (0.20 s), in orders 0 and 1, increase traversal costs at 30 s, decrease them at 90 s, and restore the initial state at 150 s. The synchronizer applies both tick-10 changes before the movement kernel advances agents, leaving no intervening movement step under the blocked state. All 2,592 successful movement runs across the main and quantity conditions finish by 11.84 s and retain exactly those two initial events. Their completion results therefore do not test sustained blocking or the later cost changes.
after: The movement experiment schedules five changes in a maximum 180 s simulated window: block one footprint and unblock a disjoint footprint at tick 10 (0.20 s), in orders 0 and 1, increase traversal costs at 30 s, decrease them at 90 s, and restore the initial state at 150 s. The synchronizer applies both tick-10 changes before advancing agents. The unblock operation does not undo the newly blocked footprint, which remains blocked during the subsequent short trajectories. All 2,592 successful movement runs across the main and quantity conditions finish by 11.84 s and retain exactly those two initial events. Their completion results therefore cover the resulting obstacle configuration but not the later cost changes.
